title: Introduce delegated RBAC audit-envelope signing and per-tenant KMS retention profiles
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: We need stronger non-repudiable audit evidence for operator-driven RBAC delegations (temporary grants, operator-on-behalf flows) and a way to control audit retention per tenant without exposing KMS keys to the control plane. This PR implements a KMS-signed audit envelope for delegated RBAC events and introduces per-tenant KMS retention profile metadata that drives downstream retention policies in the audit indexer.

What this changes: Adds a new audit envelope signer that wraps delegation events with a compact signed envelope (signed by tenant-scoped KMS / tenant key proxy), a retention_profile field propagated on tenant metadata and embedded into signed audit envelopes, and a new retention-profile-to-mlog TTL mapping used by the audit-indexer. The RBAC delegator now emits both the canonical audit event and the signed envelope for high-confidence verification by downstream compliance tooling.

Design notes: - The envelope format is intentionally compact (protobuf v3) and includes: event_id, delegation_request, actor_claims, service_context, retention_profile, signature_meta. The signature is created by the tenant KMS proxy (no plaintext key material in control plane). - Per-tenant retention_profile is a symbolic string (e.g. "standard", "sovereign-90d", "short-30d") which is validated against an allowlist during tenant onboarding and surfaced to the control plane as immutable tenant metadata. - The signer is a small, well-isolated component under services/audit/envelope to reduce blast radius; signing requests are rate-limited and retried with backoff. - Audit-indexer consumes signed envelopes and uses retention_profile to derive storage TTL; mismatches between an unsigned canonical event and a signed envelope are flagged as high-severity anomalies.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated by an ops flag (audit.envelope.enabled=false by default). 2) Deploy signer in read-only mode (emit envelopes locally to staging index) and verify consumer compatibility. 3) Enable signing for a small set of test tenants (ENG-8432) and exercise end-to-end verification. 4) Gradually flip the flag to enable for all tenants, enforcing allowlisted retention_profiles.

Backward compatibility: The canonical audit event shape is unchanged; consumers that do not understand signed envelopes will continue to ingest the unsigned event. Envelopes are published to a parallel topic (audit.envelopes.v1) so consumers can opt in.

Security considerations: - Tenant KMS usage is proxied via a tenant-escrow component that only exposes a Sign API. - Retry/backoff and rate limits prevent accidental KMS storms; the signer will fall back to emitting unsigned events with an audit annotation if signing fails for >5 minutes. - Retention profiles are validated by policy and cannot be escalated by operators without a signed change request (Linear ENG-8432).

Testing: Unit tests for envelope serialization/signature verification, integration tests that exercise the KMS proxy (mock), and an e2e test that verifies retention_profile propagation through onboarding -> delegator -> indexer. A flaky e2e test was observed in CI related to an unrelated indexer timing assumption and was retried (see CI details).

Migration and data: A migration adds tenant.retention_profile to the tenants table (nullable, default "standard"). Existing tenants will be backfilled to "standard" with a background job after rollout. Audit-indexer will interpret missing profiles as "standard".

Checklist: - [x] Schema and migration for tenant retention profile - [x] Envelope protobuf and signer implementation - [x] KMS proxy Sign API integration (mocked in unit tests) - [x] Audit-indexer TTL map and anomaly detector - [x] Docs: security/delegated_rbac_kms.md - [x] End-to-end tests and load sanity check

Related: ENG-8432 (linear), SUP-1123 (support note for test tenant), SEC-214 (threat modelling work).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Strong design. Two requests: 1) Add a mechanism to surface signing latency to the tracing spans; 2) ensure signer errors are recorded as a non-fatal metric so SRE can alert without dropping events.
Asha Menon: Added tracing instrumentation to signer (commit f6d7e2a) and added metrics.signer.failures & metrics.signer.latency. Updated docs to include operational runbook.
Priya Raman: Please validate the protobuf backward compatibility guarantees and add explicit versioning in proto namespace. Also request a short security review on the KMS proxy auth flow.
Asha Menon: Proto is namespaced audit.envelope.v1; added explicit version field in envelope.proto and recorded SEC review ticket SEC-214 in the PR. Updated tests to assert version roundtrip.
Evan Cho: Small nit—retention_profile allowlist should be configurable via infra config; otherwise LGTM.
Asha Menon: Moved allowlist into infra/config/defaults.yaml and added validation at tenant-onboard time.

release_notes: Added KMS-signed audit envelopes for delegated RBAC events and per-tenant retention_profile metadata. Feature is gated and rolled out gradually; existing audit consumers continue to work with unsigned canonical events.
notes_for_ops: Monitoring: metrics.signer.latency, metrics.signer.failures, audit.envelope.mismatch.count. Trace span: audit.envelope.sign. Fallback behaviour: after 5 minutes of consecutive signing failures signer switches to annotated unsigned events and emits ops alert.
